Insert and remove a contact ten times with the removal tool [work E5]

goal: Every resistor and diode the switch ladders use is soldered to 4 in leads, heat-shrunk, measured, labelled with its switch and position, and bagged with its measured value written on the bag.

know:
A ladder is a set of resistors on a switch so one PMU input wire can tell every switch position apart by its resistance [ladders]
Resistors come from the 1 % metal-film kit P069 [parts P069]
Each sub-assembly is checked again in the car: ohms at the plug against the table, within 2 % [work E20]
Key switch, input A16 (wire L3-S1 1): ACC 33 kΩ · IG 15 kΩ · ST 6.8 kΩ, all onto one wire [cavities L3-S1 1; ladders A16]
Light switch E-01, input A15 (L3-S1 2): PARK 33 kΩ · HEAD 15 kΩ · DIMMER-HI 8.2 kΩ · PASS 3.3 kΩ [cavities L3-S1 2; ladders A15]
Turn stalk F-02, input A1 (L3-S1 3): LEFT 1.8 kΩ · RIGHT 10 kΩ · OFF 47 kΩ [cavities L3-S1 3; ladders A1]
Wiper stalk D-03, input A2 (L3-S1 4): HIGH 4.7 kΩ · LOW 10 kΩ · INT 18 kΩ · OFF 47 kΩ [cavities L3-S1 4; ladders A2]
Wiper WASH leg: 470 Ω + 1N4148, band toward the contact - the ladders, cavity and device rows agree [ladders A2 WASH; cavities L3-S1 4; parts P161]
Brake pedal switch, input A3 (L3-S1 5): 4.7 kΩ. Wiper park, also A3 (L2-S 3): 12 kΩ at the motor's terminal L, and a 47 kΩ baseline to the front ground at the L2-S plug [cavities L3-S1 5, L2-S 3; ladders A3]
Horn pad (L3-S1 11, input A8): 8.2 kΩ [cavities L3-S1 11; ladders A8]

Gear selector (inhibitor) switch A-06: 8.2 kΩ in the lead to terminal BY (input A4, L1-S1 11) and 8.2 kΩ in the lead to GY (input A5, L1-S2 7), each with a 47 kΩ baseline to the block ground at the switch [cavities L1-S1 11, L1-S2 7; D-487]
Door jamb switches, input A6 (L4-S 2): driver 24 kΩ + 1N4148, passenger 8.2 kΩ + 1N4148, diode anodes toward the splice; a 47 kΩ baseline from the sill splice to the sill ground [cavities L4-S 2; D-486]

done_when: One labelled bag per switch position in the lists above, each with a resistor (and its diode where named) on two 4 in leads under heat-shrink, each measured within 1 % of its value and the reading written on the bag.
if_not: A part that reads outside 1 % of its marked value: bin it and make another - the in-car check allows 2 % in all. A diode that reads open both ways or short both ways: bin it. The WASH leg: if the tables still disagree when you reach it, leave it unmade and raise it in the app as a note.
record: Tick the row. Note any value you could not make (the WASH leg) in the app.

Eye protection for grinding and crimping
The Class-T fuse stays OUT all weekend
know:
The master disconnect is a Blue Sea 9003e (350 A continuous, 1500 A cranking), on the battery POSITIVE, within reach from the hatch. It carries both the PMU leg and the starter leg, so opening it kills the whole car [parts P049; D-319; work E9]
The Class-T block is a Blue Sea 5007100 with a 150 A fuse (Blue Sea 5114): the only common fuse that can break a lithium short. It mounts as close to the positive post as physically possible - inches [parts P047, P048; D-062]
C12: battery + clamp stud to the disconnect's INPUT stud, 1/0 red, 1.0 ft - a hand estimate, confirm. It is the one cable no fuse protects: keep it to inches [cables C12; D-062]
C01: the disconnect's OUTPUT stud to the Class-T block's input, 2 AWG red, 1.0 ft - a hand estimate, confirm. Its lug sits on the output stud UNDER the MRBF fuse holder that goes on at E10 [cables C01]
C05: battery - clamp stud straight to the rear ground stud, 1/0 black, 3 ft - a hand estimate, confirm. The negative is never switched [cables C05; backbone B5]
Lugs: 1/0 are P098 (3/8 in hole for the disconnect, the ground studs and the clamp studs; 5/16 for the MRBF holder), 2 AWG are P064 (5/16 and 3/8 holes) - the hole at each stud is confirm until the studs are measured [parts P098, P064, P095; checks CK24]
Rear ground stud: bare metal, a 3/8 in stainless stud (P058), a star washer (P059), torqued, cavity wax (P082) over the joint [work E9; backbone B5]
The same stud is the rear star: the table also holds a 10 AWG conductor from it to the chassis (G23, 2 ft, confirm) [grounds G23; cables C14; work E9]
Every lug gets heavy-wall adhesive shrink and a boot [work E9; parts P066, P077]
Every heavy connection is torqued to its maker's figure and paint-marked; none of the figures is in the record yet - use the ones you read at D1 [rules torque]
The positions of the switch, the block and the stud come from the M-4 mock-up; none is in the record [work V-088]
done_when: Disconnect and Class-T block mounted; rear ground stud on bare metal, waxed; C12, C01 and C05 made with a lug, heavy-wall shrink and a boot at each end, labelled; C12 and C01 bolted and torqued; C05 bolted at the stud with its battery end off and insulated; switch OFF, Class-T fuse out; meter shows continuity through the switch ON and open with it OFF.
if_not: A lug that turns on its cable or shows strands: cut it off and crimp a new one (the spares are for this). A hole that does not match its stud: stop, note the sizes, and do not drill a lug out. No continuity through the switch when ON: check each nut and the switch itself before going on.
record: Tick the row. Note the three cables' real cut lengths (C12, C01, C05) and the torque you used at each stud in the app.

goal: The factory harness takes its supply from the temporary post through its own fusible links and its ground from the front star; the Class-T and MRBF fuses are in; the battery is connected; and the Ionic app shows the pack's voltage, charge and temperature.

Spanners for the post, the stud nuts and the battery clamps
Torque wrench (P046)
Multimeter on DC volts (P045)
Ratchet crimper for insulated terminals (P171) and heat gun (P042) if a ring is needed
Phone with the Ionic app
Paint pen (from P082)

The factory harness's main feed is the black 1.25 sq main fusible link (PT317) in block X-07, with a brown 0.3 sq link either side of it (PT316) for the headlight retractors and the headlights [00-CAR PT317, PT316]
The 1985 manual places the fusible links at the front left suspension tower - 1985 manual, confirm on the car [00-CAR SP-063]
The factory feed keeps its fusible links in series on the post: nothing of the factory protection is bypassed [work E11]

The Ionic's output range is 8.0 to 14.6 V; it read 13.0 V, 3.25 V a cell, on 2026-09-08 [00-CAR SP-232; D-330]
The pack's published operating range is -20 to 60 C [00-CAR SP-233]

goal: The engine starts and runs on the new backbone, the alternator charges the Ionic at or under 14.6 V, both cranking voltage drops are entered with every joint at 0.1 V or less (D-539), and every factory circuit works exactly as before.
where: cargo bin and engine bay, the car stationary
tools:
Multimeter on DC volts (P045), with min/max hold if it has it
A long jumper lead to extend one meter probe from the cargo bin to the engine bay - not in the parts table: any light wire will do
An assistant on the key
Wheel chocks
Extinguisher within reach

E11 is done: fuses in, battery connected, the app reading
Garage door open; belt and fan clear of leads, sleeves and tools
Car in P, wheels chocked: the seats are out and it is not driven
Extinguisher within reach
know:
The factory cluster was unplugged at the strip (S1): re-plug it so the meters read; the tachometer gives you 2,000 rpm [work E12]
Charging voltage at the battery at 2,000 rpm: expect 13.8 to 14.6 V [work E12]
The Ionic's maximum charge voltage is 14.6 +/- 0.1 V. Above about 14.7 V the fix is the alternator's regulator, never the battery [checks CK03; 00-CAR SP-231]
The factory regulated band is 14.2 to 15.2 V, so a healthy factory alternator can be too high for this battery [00-CAR SP-081]
The check asks for the reading with headlights off, then with headlights and blower on, engine warm [checks CK03]
This car has shown no charge before: 11.4 V at idle. The new excitation circuit that should cure it comes at E28 (F15, migration step MG21) [D-198; work E12]
Voltage drop while cranking, battery + post to starter stud, and battery - post to engine block: each under 0.5 V; near 0.5 V means a bad crimp [work E12]
Cranking pulls 300 to 500 A briefly [backbone B2]
By the wire table 18 ft of 1/0 is about 0.0018 ohm, which by itself drops 0.5 V at about 280 A: a hard crank can read a little over 0.5 V on the cable alone - record the figure either way [awg 1/0; cables C04, C11; arithmetic]
Shut the engine down before opening the master disconnect [recovery RC01]
No driving: the interior is out until E35 [D-387]
done_when: The engine starts and idles; the battery reads between 13.8 and 14.6 V at 2,000 rpm; each cranking drop is 1.0 V or under end to end with every joint 0.1 V or less; lamps, wipers, horn, blower and the other factory circuits work as they did; the three readings are entered in E42, E43 and E44.
if_not: It does not crank: disconnect ON? MRBF in? C04 tight at both ends? It cranks but does not charge (battery voltage does not rise above the resting figure): stop running it - the alternator or its excitation is the cause, and E28 rebuilds the excitation; do not run long on the battery alone. Above 14.6 V: stop, note the figure, raise it in the app (the regulator). A drop of 0.5 V or more: find the warm or loose lug on that side and re-make it, then repeat.
record: Tick the row. Then enter E42 (V, both readings), E43 (V) and E44 (V) in their own rows.

goal: The charging voltage at the battery at 2,000 rpm is measured and entered, and it is at or under 14.6 V.

goal: The wake strip carries its seven diodes and bleed resistor, the two wake sense stages are built on the perfboard to the wake_stages table, the two bias resistors are fitted, and every check that needs no power is read on the bench. The powered checks are taken in the car.
where: bench
tools:
Soldering iron and solder (P044)
Flush cutters, needle-nose pliers (P043)
Multimeter: ohms, diode test, DC volts (P045)
Heat gun (P042)
before:
E14 - the strip and perfboard are mounted
A10 - the stage values are in the record (they are: the wake_stages table)
Eye protection while soldering and clipping leads
know:
The PMU wakes when pin 7 (+12V SW) goes high. Seven sources are OR-ed onto it through one diode each, so no source can feed another [pins 7]
Strip inputs: 1 ACC (L3-S1 12) · 2 RUN (L3-S2 1) · 3 door stage · 4 horn / hazard / wink stage · 5 O22 keep-alive (pin 8) · 6 brake plunger (L3-S1 7) · 7 DCU wake request (DP-DCU 14) [node_conductors N33-N37, N63, N76]
Seven 1N5819, band (cathode) toward the common rail; the rail goes to pin 7; 10 kΩ from the rail to the GND bus [node_conductors N38, work E15]
The two sense stages are a comparator design now: one LM2903 DIP-8 serves both, U1A the door line (A6, pin 18), U1B the horn / hazard / wink line (A8, pin 19) [wake_stages WS15, WS25; work E15]
Both stages are fed from F23, 3 A, constant from the busbar [fuses F23, node_conductors N87]
The base clamps are 1N4148, never a Schottky: a 1N5819 leaks hot and loses the pulse at 85 °C [wake_stages WS19]
The edge capacitors are 2.2 µF film (P158); the value is still to be confirmed against the PMU boot time CK12 reads [wake_stages WS17]
The threshold divider resistors WS14 / WS24 are 1 % parts [wake_stages WS14]
Bias: 100 kΩ from pin 15 (+5 V) to pin 35 (A15) and 100 kΩ from pin 15 to pin 22 (A16), so a broken wire reads 0, not OFF [node_conductors N39]
At rest the door and A8 lines sit at 0.166 x the F23 voltage (about 1.99 V at 12.0 V); the comparator threshold is 0.115 x [wake_stages WS12, WS13]
The PMU is never powered on the bench, so check CK12 is split. Here, with the meter alone: (i) the PMU's own input resistance. In the car: (ii) what pin 7 draws, at first power (E24); the A8 stage on the real horn, hazard and wink switches once L3 is plugged in (E26); the door stage on the real jamb switches once L4 is in (E27); (iii) the time from wake to O22, when O22 is first enabled (MG02 in E28) [checks CK12; D-541]
The lowest pin 7 voltage that switches the PMU on needs a variable supply, and nothing is bought to measure it: it is not taken. In the car pin 7 sees battery voltage less one strip diode [checks CK12; D-541; node_conductors N38]
LM2903 pin-out, 8 pins, pin 1 at the dot or the notch end: 1 OUT A · 2 IN- A · 3 IN+ A · 4 GND · 5 IN+ B · 6 IN- B · 7 OUT B · 8 V+ [parts P160; 00-CAR S-501]
2N3904, flat face toward you and leads down: emitter · base · collector, left to right - the usual order, not read from the sheet of the parts bought: confirm on one with the diode test before soldering [parts P072]
done_when: Seven diodes read forward toward the rail and blocked the other way; every resistor measured before fitting and again in place; no bridge between perfboard rows; CK12 (i) read on the unpowered PMU and noted.
if_not: A diode that conducts both ways or neither: replace it. A resistor out of tolerance: take another from the kit. If the unpowered PMU pin reads under 200 kΩ to ground at CK12 (i), stop: WS12 may have to drop - raise a note with the reading before the board is closed up. A stage that later does not wake in the car (E26, E27): check the comparator supply (F23) and the divider node (0.115 x F23), then the 2.2 µF and the follower - so mount the perfboard where a probe still reaches it with the node in the car.
record: Tick the row. Enter CK12 (i) as a note: ohms from pin 18 and from pin 19 to pin 25 with the PMU unpowered. The rest of CK12 is entered at E24, E26, E27 and E28.

goal: All 39 cavities of the PMU connector are terminated, locked and pull-tested, each on 18 in of labelled wire.

Eye protection

The pin list on the laptop or phone
Phone camera

goal: The sleeping current of the whole dash node, in the car on its real feed, is measured and is 50 mA or less.
where: in the car: the master disconnect in the cargo bin, and the dash node
time: 20 min, inside E24 and straight after R6 - confirm
tools:
Multimeter with a fused 10 A range and a mA range, with clip leads (P045)
Fuse puller
Notepad

The DCU tails are dust-capped

Target 30 mA or less; accept 50 mA or less [work E19, loads LD17, D-280]
The acceptance test is taken on the real node in the car at first power, not on a bench rig: where it is taken changed, the figure did not [D-541, D-280]
What should be drawing: the PMU switched off (R6's figure) and the wake stages (under 0.2 mA) on F23. K11, K14 and K15 are open when asleep. The Control Unit is not plugged in yet: its 10 mA is read at E26 [loads LD17; work R6, E26]

tools:

know:
The configuration is the record itself: names and channels from pins, states from inputs and ladders, expressions from logic, retry behaviour from rules, the bus from can_messages [work E25]
The PMU is configured here, in the car, on its real wiring - never on a bench rig. Nothing is enabled, so nothing can move while it is typed [D-541]
22 outputs. O1-O5 and O12-O16 are the 25 A pins. O6-O11 are the 15 A pins. O17-O22 are the 7 A pins: they are the analog pins A9-A14 set up as outputs [pins; inputs A9-A14]
Ten inputs. A1-A8 are the 0-5 V ladder inputs, read as 0-1023 counts. A15 and A16 are the two ladders fed from battery voltage, each with a 100 kOhm bias from pin 15 (+5 V) [rules ladder-decode; node_conductors N39]
No decode window is typed today. Windows are read live in the car at E26 and E27 and entered then [D-142]
No current limit today. The enable-at limits go in at E26 [work E25]
CAN1 is the laptop bus at 1 Mbps. CAN2 is the car's bus at 500 kbps, 11-bit ids, with the PMU's software termination ON [pins 23, 24; params can_bitrate]
The PMU's four frames 0x100, 0x110, 0x120 and 0x130 are a CANbus Export we define, byte by byte [D-378; can_fields]
Wire is control and CAN is telemetry: the only bus values the PMU acts on are the panel keys in frame 0x400 - rear defog, hatch, fuel door and the window keys [D-251; can_messages 0x400]
OIL_MIN, the oil-pressure count the fuel-pump gate compares against, is not entered today. It is read in the car at the first idle [logic FUEL_PUMP]
The pop-up cycle's idle-current threshold is not typed today either. It comes from CK08's powered readings and is entered when the pop-ups move, MG15 [rules pop-up-cycle]
The PMU has a built-in inertia switch that drops every output above a set acceleration, 6 G by default [work G3]
Saved files come back to the project by hand if they are to be kept [D-376]

know:
The order is the migration table's, by its sequence number. It is the test order: each circuit is proven alone before the next moves, so a fault shows on the circuit that caused it [work E28; D-414]
The loop for every circuit: (1) unplug the load at its factory connector, cut that harness-side plug off the old harness with 150 mm of its lead, label the stub left behind MIGRATED and the date, tape it back; (2) join the plug's leads to the new wires and plug the load back in - or fit the ring, spade or new connector its row names; (3) enable that one output at its enable-at value; (4) operate it and read the live current in the client; (5) measure voltage at the device under load; (6) record it [work E28]
Voltage test: load running, busbar to the device's + terminal under 0.5 V; the device's - terminal to the ground bus under 0.3 V [work E28]
Every leg ends in the plug its part needs, and each row below names it from the device's own row. A factory part keeps its factory plug: the harness half comes off the old harness with 150 mm of lead and each lead is joined to its new wire with a sealed heat-shrink butt splice, the splices staggered and the bundle sleeved; the two-letter factory colour says which lead takes which wire. A stud or tab takes a ring or spade; a new part takes the connector bought for it [D-537; D-543; devices plug, leg_end; rules device-end]
A plug that several circuits share - a rear lamp's one plug carries tail, stop, turn and reverse - comes off the old harness at the first of those rows. Its fuse block X-04 is under the dash. These stay together until E30 [00-CAR PT027, PT318, PT321, PT323, PT325]
Output status numbers in the client: 0 OFF, 1 ACTIVE, 2 UNDERCURRENT (a dead bulb), 3 OVERCURRENT (a tripped soft fuse), 7 THERMAL SHUTDOWN [recovery RC04]
Factory wire colours are base then tracer: GY is green with a yellow stripe; Lg is light green [00-CAR PT027]
The headlamp units in the car are LED housings fitted by a previous owner, so their current will be well under the halogen figures [00-CAR PT035]
A stalled pop-up motor pulls 15 to 25 A and the lamps move fast [work E4]
The car does not start until the last row, MG23, and is not driven until E35 [D-414; D-387]
Soft-fuse limits are set from current measured live, never from a typed guess. The measured baselines are taken at shakedown [D-025; checks CK01]
CK16 is taken after the pop-ups move and CK14 at the first crank [checks CK16, CK14]
done_when: Every migration row from MG01 to MG27 is done and each works on its own; every factory end is labelled MIGRATED with its date; the engine cranks only in P and N, starts and idles on the new harness; OIL_MIN is entered from the first idle; CK14 and CK16 are logged; a new revision is saved.
if_not: A circuit does not come up: stop there - the fault is in what you just moved. Read that output's status in the client: 3 means a shorted wire - find it, do not raise the limit; 2 means an open load or a dead bulb; no current and status 0 means the input state is wrong - watch the ladder while you work the switch. Low voltage at the device: the feed's crimp or splice. Voltage on the ground side: the ring or the star stud. Once its plug is cut off the old harness the circuit cannot simply go back: look for the fault on the new side first. A plug found cracked, burnt, or not what its device row says: do not splice it on - raise it in the app as a note; a new connector is bought for that part instead (D-543). For a PMU soft fault use recovery RC02 to RC05.
record: Tick E28 in the app when MG23 has moved and the engine has run. E2 takes the odometer reading before MG22. The per-circuit current and voltage readings, CK14's lowest cranking voltage and block offset, and CK16's readings have no row of their own: put them in a note in the app.

goal: Every circuit has been worked in one pass - key out, ACC, RUN and engine running - on the new harness alone, the limp-home procedure has been proven once, the configuration is saved as a new revision, and the whole car draws 50 mA or less asleep.
where: the whole car, in the garage with the door open; the dash node for the limp-home test; the cargo bin for the sleep reading
time: half a day, plus an hour's wait for the sleep reading - confirm
tools:
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
clamp meter that reads DC milliamps, or the multimeter in series at the disconnect
the limp-home kit: three fused jumpers 10 A, 20 A and a 5 A one with a pushbutton, a work light, the printed recovery table (P139)
a stopwatch, to time the limp-home procedure
a helper to watch the lamps at the rear
before:
E28 done: every migration row moved, the engine has started and idled
Wheels chocked; the car is not driven (the interior is out until E35)
Garage door open whenever the engine runs; belt and fan clear

know:
The check is one pass through four key states: key out, ACC, RUN, engine running [work E29]
With the key out these still work, each by waking the PMU first: hazards, horn, each wink, brake lamps, and the interior and courtesy lamps on their own fuses [rules flasher; pins 7; fuses F12, F19]
The car goes back to sleep 30 s after the last change with the key out, both doors shut and nothing pressed. Hazards hold it awake with no limit [logic KEEP_ALIVE]
Wipers: when switched off they run on to the park position; INT is one sweep and a 3 s pause; a flick of LOW under 400 ms is one sweep; the washer pump runs only while WASH is held, then two more sweeps [rules wiper-park, washer]
Flasher rate 1.5 Hz. The hazard switch overrides the stalk [rules flasher]
Dash illumination is on with PARK and HEAD and dims; the interior lamp is on its own door switch with the key out [D-462]
The starter runs only with the lever in P or N [rules crank]
Limp-home, dead module: the PMU's 39-way is unplugged and three fused jumpers run from the busbar - 10 A onto relay K13 terminal 30 for the fuel pump, 20 A onto the O12 splice for ignition, and a 5 A pushbutton jumper onto K9's terminal 86 lead to crank, lever in P [recovery RC07]
On the jumpers the key still stops the engine by dropping K13, but there is no oil gate and no inhibitor: ignition is live whenever the disconnect is closed [recovery RC08]
If the limp-home takes more than about twenty minutes in a warm garage it will not happen at the roadside in the rain [checks CK11]
Sleeping current: 50 mA or under is accepted, 30 mA is the target. On the 40 Ah pack 150 mA is about 11 days of parking and 20 mA about 80 [checks CK02; loads LD17; D-280]
The pack gives no slow-crank warning: it is fine, then it is dead at 8.0 V [checks CK02]
done_when: Every function in the steps works first time in its key state and nothing works in a state where it should not; the engine starts and runs on the limp-home jumpers and everything is restored after; the new revision is saved in the PMU, on the laptop and on the copy for the car; one hour after key-off the car draws 50 mA or less.
if_not: A function fails: it is that circuit's migration row again - status in the client, then the ladder state, then the voltage at the device. Limp-home does not start the engine: the procedure is wrong, and now is when to find out - note exactly which jumper and which terminal failed. Sleep reading over 50 mA: with the meter still in place pull, one at a time, F1 (head unit memory), F19 (courtesy lamps), F22 (Control Unit), F23 (wake stages), F12 (interior lamp), and watch for the drop; the pack's own BMS is the remainder. Do not go on to E30 on a failing sleep number.
record: Tick E29 in the app. No value on this row. The sleep reading in mA and the limp-home time in minutes have no row of their own: put both in a note.

goal: The whole factory harness is out of the car in one piece - with its fuse box, relays, control unit and the factory cluster - boxed and kept as the fallback, and the car still works on the new harness alone.
where: the whole car: under the dash, the engine bay, the left sill and the rear
tools:
sockets, spanners and screwdrivers for the harness clips and the fuse box - sizes are not in the record
trim clip tool
label printer (P041) or tags, for each connector as it comes out
camera
a box big enough to coil the harness without kinking it
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
before:
E29 passed: the full function check, the limp-home test and the sleep reading
Every migration row done and every factory end labelled MIGRATED with its date
The interior is still out (D-387, D-411)
Master disconnect OPEN before the factory main feed is taken off the busbar

The harness comes out INTACT. It is not cut anywhere. It is the fallback if something fails in shakedown, and refitting it is a big job [work E30; D-411]
It leaves with the factory fuse box, the relays, the control unit and the factory cluster [work E30; D-268]
The factory harness is several harnesses joined by big connectors: the front harness with the fuse block; the engine harness at X-01, a 22-cavity plug; the dash harness at X-02 and X-12; the rear harness at X-03, on the left side behind the door - check; the transmission harness at X-10, a 6-pin, and X-17, two 1-pins; the parking-brake harness at X-11 [00-CAR PT309, PT321, PT325, PT318, PT323]
The factory cluster is on two 13-cavity round connectors [00-CAR PT614]
The control unit is the box that did the flasher, the intermittent wipers and the warning chimes. The PMU does all of that now [00-CAR PT301]
The factory body grounds are X-13, at the left suspension tower and under the dash on the left, and X-14 and X-15, whose places are not in the record: follow the black wires [00-CAR PT027]

What stays: every device and switch the new harness uses - lamps, motors, senders, the column switches, the horn pad, the parking-brake switch, the kick-down switch and solenoid, the two release solenoids - and the wideband gauge at the node [devices; D-244]
The A/C stays as it is: compressor on the car, clutch unplugged, belt off, the rest untouched [D-474]
There is no week of driving on the old harness: the car is not driven until the interior is back [work E30]
done_when: No factory wire, fuse box, relay or control unit is left in the car; the harness is in its box in one piece with every connector labelled; nothing the new harness uses was disturbed; the car starts and every function still works.
if_not: Something is still plugged into the factory harness that no migration row moved: stop. Label it, photograph it, and raise it in the app as a note before unplugging it - it is a circuit the design does not know about. A connector that will not part: do not cut the wire; note it. A function that stopped working after the harness came out was sharing a factory ground or feed: find it now, while the harness is still in the garage.
record: Tick E30 in the app. No value. A note listing anything found still connected, and where the box is kept.

goal: The factory odometer's reading is entered in the app, in miles, before the factory cluster goes dark.
where: at the factory cluster - loose in the car with the dash out, still plugged in since E12
tools:
phone camera
a torch
before:
F3 done: the new display proven on the bench - this row's gate
Take it before E28 starts: E28 is gated on this row
know:
The factory cluster stays alive on the factory harness until the meters cutover, MG22, then goes dark and leaves the car with that harness [D-268]
The new instrument unit keeps its own odometer and starts it from this figure [work E2; D-269]
The new odometer is stored in the unit's own memory every 0.1 mile, with the memory card as a second copy, so a missing card cannot lose the mileage [D-269]
The speedometer is cable-driven, with a trip reset knob [00-CAR PT621]
The car is not driven between the strip and E35, so the figure does not change before the cutover [work E12]
The reply is a value in miles [work E2]
done_when: The reading is saved on this row in the app and a photo of the odometer exists.
if_not: A digit sits between two numbers or cannot be read: photograph it and enter the lower figure, with a note. The cluster has already been unplugged: the odometer is part of the cable-driven speedometer head, so it should still read with no power - confirm, and take it off the cluster wherever it is.
record: Enter the odometer reading on this row, in miles. Nothing else.

goal: The time from pressing the horn pad on a sleeping car to the horn sounding is measured and entered in milliseconds.
where: driver's seat and the nose of the car
tools:
a stopwatch and a helper
a phone filming in slow motion, if you want a figure finer than a thumb can give
before:
E25 done: the PMU configured - this row's gate
The horn has moved to the new harness (MG04 in E28)
Key out, both doors shut, nothing pressed for at least 30 s, so the PMU is asleep
know:
The horn, hazards, winks and the brake lamps all work with the key out, and all of them work by waking the PMU first: a wake stage lifts pin 7, the PMU boots, reads the switch and drives the output [work Q-110; pins 7]
Nothing in the design says how long that takes, and the horn's whole value is in its first 200 ms [work Q-110]
Under about 200 ms: nothing more to do. Over about 500 ms: the question becomes whether the horn should hang off the always-hot busbar through its own relay - a change this build can still absorb [work Q-110]
The brake lamps are the same measurement and matter more [work Q-110; D-278]
Item (iii) of check CK12 - the time from pin 7 going high to O22 coming on - was read at MG02 in E28, in the car: compare [checks CK12; D-541]
The PMU sleeps 30 s after the last input change with the key out and the doors shut [logic KEEP_ALIVE]
done_when: A figure in ms is entered for the horn, taken from a car that was truly asleep, and the brake-lamp delay is noted beside it.
if_not: It sounds instant and cannot be timed by hand: film the press and the horn in slow motion and count frames; if it still cannot be resolved enter your best estimate and say in a note that it is a ceiling, not a measurement. Over 500 ms: enter the figure and stop - the fix is a design change, not an adjustment.
record: Enter the horn delay on this row in ms. Add the brake-lamp delay in a note. Q-028 takes the same measurement cold.

goal: The wake-to-horn delay with the car cold is on record, in milliseconds, so it never has to be found again.
where: driver's seat and the nose of the car, on a cold morning
tools:
a stopwatch and a helper, or a phone filming in slow motion
an outdoor thermometer
before:
E25 done: the PMU configured - this row's gate
The horn on the new harness (MG04 in E28)
The car left asleep overnight in the cold
know:
Nothing depends on this number today. It is recorded in case the horn or the winks ever move to a wake sent over the CAN bus [work Q-028]
The question it answers: what wake-to-horn delay is acceptable cold [work Q-028]
It is the same measurement as Q-110, taken cold [work Q-028, Q-110]
The wake stages must hold their rest state cold as well as warm. Check CK12 asks for a cold reading too, and nothing was read on a bench: this cold morning is where it is taken [checks CK12; D-541]
done_when: A figure in ms is entered, with the air temperature in a note.
if_not: The horn does not sound at all from a cold sleep: that is a fault in the wake stage, not a slow reading - note it at once and check 12 V on pin 7 while the pad is held.
record: Enter the cold wake-to-horn delay on this row in ms. Air temperature in a note.

goal: The hatch and the fuel door each open from their key on the left plate: relays K3 and K4 are in their sockets, fuse F33 is in, both solenoids are on the new harness with a proven ground, and each solenoid's current has been read.
where: dash node (K3, K4, F33); the hatch latch; behind the driver-side rear quarter trim (the fuel-door solenoid)
tools:
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
an ammeter or clamp meter that reads 20 A DC
a fused 12 V test lead
ratchet crimper for heat-shrink butt splices and rings (P171)
heat gun (P042)
label printer (P041)
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
before:
E22 done: the rear leg built, with L4-M 3 and L4-M 4 run to the two solenoids
A11 done: the release design, including the hatch latch switch. If A11 is still open, this row's gate is not met
The Control Unit and the left plate plugged in (E26), O10 migrated (MG02 in E28)
Master disconnect OPEN while relays, the fuse and the solenoid ends are fitted
know:
Both solenoids are the car's own. They exist and are believed to work; nobody has tested them on the new harness [devices DV48, DV49]
Factory wires: the hatch solenoid has GR (+) and B; the fuel-door solenoid has GB (+) and B. Each B went to the rear body ground [00-CAR PT030, PT031]
New feed, hatch: L4-M 3, 14 AWG orange, from relay K3 terminal 87, through the hatch hinge loop with the tail-lamp wires, to the solenoid's + [cavities L4-M 3; relays K3]
New feed, fuel door: L4-M 4, 14 AWG orange, from relay K4 terminal 87, behind the quarter trim, to the solenoid's + [cavities L4-M 4; relays K4]
Each solenoid's - stays on its factory ground at the body. Prove it with the meter [devices DV48, DV49]
K3 and K4 are ordinary micro relays in sockets at the dash node, labelled HATCH-REL and FUEL-REL. Terminals 30 and 86 of both are fed from O10 through F33, a 10 A sealed inline fuse. Terminal 85 of K3 goes to the Control Unit on DP-DCU 24, and K4's to DP-DCU 25: the Control Unit grounds one to pick which opens [relays K3, K4; fuses F33]
The relays have power whenever O10 is on, not only during a release. What stops a stray release is F33, pull-downs in the Control Unit, and its firmware: it refuses unless the car is stopped and lets go after 1.5 s at most [D-465]
With the key off a release is allowed when the PMU reports the key OFF and no road speed is seen [work A11]
The two keys are on the left plate, left of the steering wheel. The Control Unit sends them in frame 0x400: byte 0 bit 1 hatch, bit 2 fuel door [cavities DP-DCU 37, DP-DCU 38; can_fields 0x400/0]
Nobody knows what the solenoids draw. The factory fuse for them was 20 A; F33 is 10 A; O10 trips at 13 A and already carries up to 10 A [checks CK20; 00-CAR SP-218]
The hatch latch switch is broken. Its replacement is P165, bought once the car confirmed the switch is what failed. Where its wires land is A11's and is not in the tables yet - confirm [parts P165; work A11]
done_when: Pressing the hatch key opens the hatch and pressing the fuel-door key opens the fuel door, key at ACC and with the key out; neither opens by itself when the key is turned on; each solenoid's current is known; F33 is still intact after ten releases of each.
if_not: A solenoid does not pull: 12 V at its + during the press? If yes, its ground or the solenoid itself; if no, listen for the relay - a click with no voltage is F33 or the 87 wire, no click is the select line from the Control Unit (DP-DCU 24 or 25) or the key not reaching the bus. F33 blows: the current reading says why; do not fit a bigger fuse - note the reading, the rating is revised from it. A solenoid that fires when the key is turned on: stop, pull F33, and note it.
record: Tick E36 in the app. No value on this row. The two solenoid currents in amps go in a note: they are CK20's reading and may change F33.

time: one day for both doors - confirm
tools:
Deutsch solid-contact crimper, sizes 12 and 16 (P038)
contact removal tool, size 16 (P031)
ratchet crimper for heat-shrink butt splices and rings (P171)
heat gun (P042)

a stiff pull wire for the jamb boot

E22 done: the sill node built, D1 and D2 pinned on the node side
A12 done: the door harness drawn, which needs the mirror measured at its plug (luxury W-332). If either is still open, this row's gate is not met
Master disconnect OPEN
Window glass fully up and taped before the trim comes off

D1 is the driver door's 8-way Deutsch plug and D2 the passenger's; both mate receptacles at the sill node. The run from the sill node into each door goes through the jamb boot; the 3D model estimates 7.5 ft, measured at M-2 [housings D1, D2; routes RT20]
Cavities, the same in both: 1 window motor leg A, 14 AWG red - 2 window motor leg B, 14 AWG red - 3 a sealing plug, stays - 4 mirror motor common, 16 AWG grey - 5 mirror motor, 16 AWG grey - 6 mirror clutch coil, 16 AWG grey - 7 mirror heat, 16 AWG red - 8 door ground, 16 AWG black [cavities D1 1-8, D2 1-8]
Until today the door plugs hold sealing plugs in every cavity. They come out here, except cavity 3 [work E37; cavities D1 3]
Each mirror is one reversing motor plus a clutch coil that picks the axis; both mirrors share the common. Which mirror lead takes which cavity is confirm until the mirror is measured [dcu_channels SN17; cavities L4-S2 1]
The mirror heads are the car's own and keep their factory plugs. Factory mirror leads are Lg, LgB, LgY (LgR on the right) and B [work A12; 00-CAR PT032]
The window-motor legs end in a Deutsch plug at the motor's place, sized to 14 AWG. The motor's own adapter lead is a later row [work A12; D-473]

Door trim comes off in this order: window winder handle, inner handle cover, arm rest, trim panel, then the plastic water shield [S-002 p.14-9]
That page is the 1985 manual - confirm on the car [S-002 p.14-9]
The regulators and mirrors themselves are fitted later by the luxury package [work E37]
The mirror heads and the window motors are not rows of the devices table, so no plug is written down for either. goal: The comfort fuse block is mounted behind the centre stack and plugged into L3-CMF, the four under-seat receptacles are in place and capped, and the seat returns, the comfort supply and the three grounds fill cavities 1-8 of the Control Unit's one plug - every seat wire tested and waiting for the seats.

tools:
Deutsch solid-contact crimper, sizes 12 and 16 (P038)
contact removal tool, size 16 (P031)
ratchet crimper for heat-shrink butt splices and rings (P171)
heat gun (P042)
label printer (P041)
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
a 12 V test lamp
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
torque wrench 1/4 in drive, 2-20 N-m (P046)

E20 done: the dash leg L3 built, with the L3-CMF receptacle behind the centre stack
A13 and A14 done (they are): the comfort block and the seat harness designed
The Control Unit in its opening (E26)
Carpet still out: these runs go under it
Master disconnect OPEN while anything is mounted, pinned or fused
know:
The comfort block is a six-way blade fuse block with a cover and one input stud. It takes its power from output O15 through L3-CMF, a DTP 2-way receptacle behind the centre stack: cavity 1 is the feed on 12 AWG red, cavity 2 a sealing plug [parts P164; cavities L3-CMF 1, L3-CMF 2]

The record gives the four seat return wires two colours: blue at the seat receptacle, black at the Control Unit's plug. Go by continuity and the labels, not colour [cavities L3-SD 3; cavities DP-DCU 1]
Routes: from the centre stack down the tunnel side and under the carpet to each seat. Place the receptacles so the carpet comes up once [routes RT27, RT28; housings L3-SDM]
O15 COMFORT is on with the key at RUN and is shed with the other comfort loads on low voltage. It has no enable-at figure in the record - confirm [logic COMFORT; pins 27]
Everything here is built for the worst case of seats not yet chosen: heat 5 A, cooling 2.5 A, motors 10 to 20 A [devices DV57; fuses F35]

record: Tick E38 in the app. No value. Note the limit you gave O15, since the record has none.

ratchet crimper for heat-shrink butt splices and rings (P171)

A15 done (it is): the servo leads designed
Dash still out: the heater case is reachable
Master disconnect OPEN while pinning and splicing

goal: The car has been driven cold, at night, in the wet and on one long run with the log recording, and the log shows no fault, no tripped output and no channel near its limit.
where: on the road; the garage before and after each drive
time: four drives over a week or more - they wait on the weather
tools:
phone with the Rx7 app, to pull each drive's log from the instrument unit
phone with the battery's own app, to watch the pack
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
the limp-home kit and the printed recovery table in the car from the first drive (P139)
warning beacons
before:
E35 done: the interior is back
E30 done: the factory harness is out. It stays boxed until this shakedown is passed
The laptop, cable and limp-home kit ride in the car on every one of these drives
Know recovery RC01 by heart before the first drive: the master disconnect is the only certain off
know:
Four conditions: a cold start on a cold morning; a night drive; a wet drive; a long drive. Logging on for all of them [work E31]
The instrument unit writes every drive to its card: a thinned record once a second of every channel, and the full bus log. The app pulls the thinned log over Bluetooth, an hour's drive in under a minute [log_channels; params log_pull_s_per_hour; D-493]
Battery voltage: charging should sit between 13.8 and 14.6 V. The pack's ceiling is 14.6 V; the factory regulator's own band reaches 15.2 V, so watch the top. The PMU warns below 12.0 V and above 15.0 V [work E42; checks CK03; 00-CAR SP-081; rules voltage]
Cranking sags to about 10.5 V. Loads are shed only after about 10 s under 11.5 V and never during START, so the display must not reboot on a crank [rules voltage; D-463]
The pack heats itself in the cold only from a charging source; how much it draws is not published. That is what to watch in the battery app on the cold morning [00-CAR SP-233]
Per-channel current is logged for all 22 outputs. Each channel's peak is compared with its limit [log_channels LC15; work E31]
Limits in the record's own figures: water temperature 105 C, oil pressure 1.0 bar low mark, redline 7000 rpm [params hot_water_c, low_oil_bar, redline_rpm]
Fault channels that must stay zero: global fault, trip state, input faults; and CAN health must stay good [log_channels LC05, LC14, LC09, LC26]
Stuck-on check: commanded off, each of O2, O3, O5, O7 and O12 must read zero volts. Battery volts on an output that is off is a shorted switch, and only the master disconnect kills it [checks CK07]
Ground offset between the engine block and the dash ground bus should be under 50 mV, idling and at full electrical load [checks CK05]
An engine that starts and dies about 3 s later with zero oil pressure shown is the oil gate doing its job, not a PMU fault [recovery RC02]
With a dead module the car has no lights, wipers or horn: a limp home is daylight, dry and short. If stopped and dark, beacons out first [recovery RC09]
done_when: All four drives are done; each one's log is in the app; no drive shows a fault flag, a tripped or retrying output, an input fault or a lost bus; charging stayed at or under 14.6 V; every channel's peak is under its limit; the stuck-on and ground-offset checks pass.
if_not: A fault on the road: recovery RC01 first - stop, engine off, disconnect open - then RC02 to tell a soft fault from a dead module. A tripped channel: do not raise its limit on the roadside beyond what gets you home, and write down what you changed (RC05). Charging above 14.6 V: stop the shakedown - the fix is the alternator's regulator, never the battery. Ground offset over 50 mV: note it; it decides a sensor return wire at the engine swap. Anything that fails in a way the new harness cannot be made to cure: the boxed factory harness is the fallback, and that is a decision to raise in the app, not to take alone.
record: Tick E31 in the app when all four drives are logged. No value. The drives themselves are logged from the app; the stuck-on and ground-offset readings go in a note.

goal: Every output's steady current has been measured live and written down, every limit that was still at its channel cap is set from a measurement, and the configuration is saved as a new revision.
where: in the garage: laptop on DP-DIAG, engine running for the lamp and charging readings
tools:
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
pen and paper or the phone, for one figure per output
a helper to work switches
before:
E31 done: the four shakedown drives logged
Garage door open; wheels chocked; belt and fan clear
Stand clear of the pop-ups and the wiper arms while they are cycled
know:
Limits are set from current measured live in the client, never from a typed guess [D-025]
The class factors: motors, stall current x 1.1; lamps, running current x 1.35; resistive loads, cold current x 1.2; electronics, running current x 1.5 [work E32]
How to take each baseline: lamps warm, after two seconds, not the switch-on surge; motors mid-travel, not stalled [checks CK01]
A reading more than about 20 percent under the expected figure is a tired part, not a bad reading: that gap is the replacement list. A reading over the expected figure is a fault to find before the limit is set [checks CK01]
Expected running amps: O1 9.5 - O2 7.4 - O3 8.9 - O4 11.5 - O5 2.0 - O6 4.4 - O7 3.9 - O8 4.0 - O9 5.5 - O10 10.0 - O11 6.0 - O12 10 - O17 4.2 - O18 4.2 - O19 3.9 - O20 1.5 - O21 0.2 - O22 0.2 [pins est_a]
The headlamps are LED units a previous owner fitted, so O2 and O3 will read far under the halogen figures. That is the lamp, not a fault [00-CAR PT035]
Limits still at the channel's cap: O1 25.0, O4 25.0, O8 13.0, O9 13.0, O10 13.0, O11 13.0, O12 25.0, O19 7.0, O20 7.0, O21 7.0, O22 7.0. O2 and O3 sit at 13.0, the 14 AWG branch's ceiling. Already set from a measurement: O5 4.0, O6 7.5, O7 11, O17 4.5, O18 4.5 [pins enable_a, enable_basis]
No limit may go above what the pin and wire carry: 25 A pins, 15 A pins, 7 A pins; 13 A on the headlamp branches [pins hw_max_a; D-243]
Pop-up stall was measured at 12.8 and 13.1 A per side. Both on O1 is 25.9 A, and x 1.1 is 28.5 A - above the pin - so O1 stays at 25.0 [loads LD08; pins 38]
Wiper stall is a design range, 12 to 20 A, never measured [loads LD07]
O21 and O22 sit under the PMU's own measuring floor: expect zero, record zero, give them no band [checks CK01]
Health band: a lamp channel warns below half its baseline, a motor channel above one and a half times it. The low half is the PMU's Min Current setting, which only warns and never switches off. A channel whose baseline is under four times the pin's measuring floor gets no band [rules health-band]
done_when: One steady figure is written down for every live output; every limit that can be set from a measurement has been; each output has been worked again from cold and none trips; the new revision is saved in the PMU, on the laptop and on the car's copy.
if_not: A baseline over the expected figure: find the fault before setting any limit from it. A channel trips after its limit is tightened: the factor was applied to a warm reading or the inrush window is too short - go back to the previous limit, read again, and note it. A channel whose class is not obvious (the horn, ignition, the relay coils, the comfort bus): the record does not say - leave it at its cap and note it rather than guess.
record: Tick E32 in the app. No value on this row. Send the measured current for each output in a note, one line per output: it becomes the baseline and the measured figure in the record.

tools:
torque wrench 1/4 in drive, 2-20 N-m (P046), and a larger one for the battery posts and the starter stud

The legs pass the firewall on the passenger side (engine leg) and the cowl (front leg); the heavy cables and the rear leg run in the tunnel [routes RT01, RT06, RT15]

done_when: Every stud on the list is at its maker's torque with a fresh paint mark; both cranking drops are 1.0 V or under end to end with every joint 0.1 V or less, and no worse than at E12; the engine-bay looms are wrapped, clipped and clear of heat and moving parts; every grommet is seated and sealed; the car starts and charges as before.
if_not: A nut that turns a long way before it reaches torque was loose: look at the lug and the stud for heat marks, and note which one. On the 40 Ah pack that is about 11 days of parking at 150 mA against about 80 days at 20 mA, before the battery's own protection cuts off at 8.0 V with no slow-crank warning first. [D-280; 00-CAR SP-232]
The whole car asleep must be 30 mA or under, 50 mA at most; that is measured at E29. This reading is the PMU's share of it; E19, straight after, is the whole node's. [checks CK02; D-280; work E19]
Power reaches the PMU on its M6 stud, from the always-hot busbar on a short 2 AWG link. Ground is pin 25. Pin 7 (+12 V SW) switches it on and off. [pins STUD, 25, 7; cables C10; S-028 p.8]
By default the PMU switches off at once when pin 7 loses its 12 V, and before E25 no configuration holds it awake. [S-028 p.131]
At E24 the PMU is woken by the wake jumper - the second fuse holder of the P073 pair, 3 A, from the always-hot busbar to wake-strip screw 6 - and switched off by pulling that jumper's fuse. [work E24; node_conductors N63, N38]
With the master disconnect OPEN, a meter across its two studs carries everything the node draws; the 5 A guard at the Class-T block is still in series behind it. A meter in series at the disconnect is the same method the whole-car check uses. [checks CK02; work E24]
To read the PMU alone the other always-hot branches at the node are opened: F23 (the wake stages), F22 (the Control Unit's constant feed), F12 (the interior lamp) and the MAXI fuse F30 that feeds block A. K11, K14 and K15 are open with the PMU off, so F31, F35 and F36 carry nothing. [fuses F23, F22, F12, F30; relays K11, K14, K15]
Status LED: steady green means active with no PC, steady orange means active and connected to the PC. [S-028 p.14]

What is left is the PMU itself: enter it - a high figure is a finding, not a mistake. A reading that jumps about: a clip is slipping on a stud. Never close the disconnect or refit the wake fuse while the meter is on its mA range.

goal: With the PMU powered in the car and its Windows client on the glovebox port, you have found out which parts of the frames 0x100-0x130 the client can build, and told the agent; the three client checks CK06, CK13 and CK15 are read in the same sitting, before the configuration is entered.
where: in the car: the laptop on the passenger side, plugged into DP-DIAG in the glovebox
tools:
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client installed (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface the client supports: Ecumaster USBtoCAN, Peak PCAN-USB or Kvaser (P138)
a charger on the battery, or an eye on its voltage: the node is live for hours with the engine off
a notepad: you are recording what the client accepts and refuses
before:
E24 done: the node is in the car on the Class-T fuse and the PMU answers over DP-DIAG
The wake jumper from E24 is on with its 3 A fuse in: with no leg plugged in it is what keeps the PMU awake
No leg plugged in. Every output disabled, and it stays that way

know:
This proof moved from the bench into the car: the PMU is powered and set up on its real wiring, never on a rig. [D-541]
If the client cannot build a frame as designed, the fallback is simpler frames - one byte per field, fixed frames in place of 0x130's index - made in our own firmware. No wire changes either way. [D-541; D-378]
The PMU sends CAN frames two ways. Its Standard CAN Stream is fixed by ECUMaster. Its CANbus Export is ours to define, and 0x100-0x130 are Exports. [D-378; S-028 p.90, p.95]
An Export field can be 8-bit unsigned, 8-bit signed, 16-bit big endian or 16-bit little endian, times a whole multiplier from 1 to 1000, or the raw value. A frame is 0 to 8 bytes, sent 1 to 100 times a second or on an edge. [S-028 p.90-92]
The manual shows no bit-packing, no multiplexing and no rolling counter on an Export. Those three are what this row proves or rules out. [D-378]
Our four frames go out on CAN2 at 500 kbps, little-endian: 0x100 vehicle state at 20 Hz, 0x110 power at 10 Hz, 0x120 outputs at 5 Hz, 0x130 per-channel current at 5 Hz. [can_messages 0x100, 0x110, 0x120, 0x130; params can_bitrate; can_map.h]
The laptop talks to the PMU on CAN1 through DP-DIAG, the 4-way port in the glovebox: cavity 1 CAN1 high, 2 CAN1 low, 3 +12 V through F2, 4 ground. Both 120 ohm terminators are already there, one in the port and one at the PMU's connector. [cavities DP-DIAG 1-4; node_conductors N56; S-028 p.36-38]
Never connect the interface's +5 V to anything on the car. [S-028 p.37]
One extra the control panel wants if the client can export it: input A8's decoded state (idle, horn, hazard, wink L, wink R). Bytes 5-6 of 0x110 are kept for it. O20 has no duty to export: it is on/off, and the dash-light level is the Control Unit's own [work F-009; D-492; D-577]
The client is only on the Windows laptop; files it saves come back to the project by hand. [D-376]
The bytes are first seen on the wire by the two units themselves: the Control Unit reads 0x100 from E26, and the Display Unit's diagnostics page lists the frames once it boots at MG02 in E28. Today the question is only what the client will build. [work E26, E28; migration MG02]
done_when: For each of these you can say yes or no, with what the client showed: a packed bitfield byte, a rolling 0-255 counter in byte 7, a multiplexed 0x130, the two panel extras; and CK06, CK13 and CK15 each have an answer.
if_not: The client cannot do something: that is a result, not a failure. Write exactly what it offered instead, build the simpler form (one byte per field; fixed frames for 0x130) and carry on into E25 with it. The client will not connect: check about 60 ohm across DP-DIAG cavities 1 and 2 with the power off, that the two CAN wires are not swapped, and that the PMU's LED is lit - if it is dark, the wake jumper's fuse. Do not change any other setting in the PMU to make an Export work.
