It lists the pieces in this order: horn cap, nut, steering wheel, column covers, combination switch, grilles, brake cover, coin box, rear console, switch panels, ventilator louver, shift lever knob, glove box lid and compartment, ash tray, knobs, centre panel, radio, clock, heater wire, garnishes, meter hood, cluster switch, meter, then bolts and the instrument panel. [S-002 p.14-2]
The cluster is held by spring nuts and joins the car through two round 13-cavity connectors (X-05 and X-06) and the speedometer cable. [00-CAR PT614, PT621, PT622]
Each seat sits on two slide adjusters bolted to the floor. The seat bolts' torque is not in the record. [S-002 p.14-3]
The driver's seat-belt buckle carries the belt-warning switch, wires Br and BrW. [00-CAR PT908]
Steering wheel nut 40-50 N-m; mark the wheel and the shaft before it comes off. Seat-belt anchor bolts 39-55 N-m (1985 figure). [00-CAR SP-174, PT469, SP-187]
The shift knob screws onto the lever against a lock nut. The shift indicator panel is lit by a bulb on plug E-07. [00-CAR PT412, PT854]
The factory amplifier is expected behind the head unit - check; it and the factory speaker wire leave with the old harness later, not now. [00-CAR PT660; D-236]
The wideband gauge taps the factory harness at a point nobody has found. A previous owner spliced the dash badly. Photograph the tap and every splice; leave them wired. [00-CAR PT028; D-236]
Dash plug codes from the 1982 diagram, for the labels: cluster X-05 and X-06; headlamp retractor switch E-02; rear defrost switch G-24; hatch release switch H-13; fuel-door switch H-15; clock H-10; lighter H-09; radio G-04; amplifier G-08; glove box lamp H-01 and its switch H-02; blower switch G-15. [00-CAR circuits OEM-RECORD; 00-CAR PT034, PT036, PT635, PT849, PT631, PT655, PT660, PT832, PT218]
The air conditioning is not opened: a shop recovers the refrigerant before any A/C line or the compressor is disturbed. [00-CAR PR-001]
Photos go in 00-CAR/photos, one folder per zone (engine, front, dash, rear, doors, grounds, hacks), named date_zone_subject.jpg. They are the only record of the factory harness once it is out. [00-CAR photos README]
The fuel door's manual release is behind the left rear speaker cover or under the cargo carpet: a slide at the top of the mechanism pushed rearward. [00-CAR PT031]
done_when: The cabin is bare to the floor and the firewall, the cargo bins are open, no wire has been cut, every parted plug carries a matching label on both halves, every fastener is in a labelled bag, the photos are in 00-CAR/photos, and each of the 13 devices in the LOOK steps has its ways, colour and mark written down.
if_not: A panel will not come: stop pulling and look for one more fastener - the count for each panel is not in the record. A plug that will not part: leave it joined, photograph it and count its wires from the back. A wire in the way: move the panel, never the wire. A part in a LOOK step that is not there, or has no plug at all (wires soldered or screwed straight on): write exactly that. Anything you break or find already broken: photograph it and write it in the app as a note.
record: Tick S1. In words: the odometer reading, anything broken or surprising, how many previous-owner splices you found, and the plug list - one line per device id - ways, colour, any mark, which half is on the part, the photo's name, and whether the plug is sound or cracked. The agent files each line in that device's row with the date.

goal: The measurement day is done: every harness run is measured for its bundle, the water paths are looked at, the pins are counted on the used-only parts, the speedo boss thread is read, and the rows that own the other measurements are answered.
where: the whole car, interior out
tools:
tape measure
a ball of string and masking tape
calipers, and a thread gauge or known nuts
torch, phone camera and a ruler
cardboard, a knife and a marker
multimeter
jack, jack stands and wheel chocks for the under-car part
notepad with the 32 runs listed
before:
S1 is done: the interior is out
Battery negative disconnected
Nothing is cut and no panel is made until every number is in
Car on jack stands with the wheels chocked before you go under it
know:
This is the one day the car is apart for measuring. Each measurement with a number of its own has its own row in the app: the dash spaces Q-014, the sill V-055, the cargo bins V-088, the wire colours A5, the speed signal Q-115, the pop-ups V-081, the releases V-112, the head unit and wideband taps V-116. [work C1, S1]
No opening behind the dash is measured for a unit to fit: the dash is rebuilt around the units. Q-014's spaces are for the dash node and the runs, not for the Display Unit or the Control Unit. [D-542]
This row holds what has no row of its own: the routes (M-2), the water look, the pin counts, the speedo boss, and the rest of the photographs. [work C1]
There are 32 runs, RT01 to RT32, each with its measured length still blank. Lengths are in feet. Wire is cut at 1.5 times the measured run, and the whole wire order is worked out from these numbers. [routes; work G13]
The 3D model's guesses, as a sanity check only: dash post to nose 11.4 ft, across to a headlamp 3.4, front lamps 6.1, tunnel to the rear 7.7, tail lamps 9.1, hatch 7.8, sill 3.8, sill to a door 7.5. A tape always beats them. [routes RT06, RT07, RT08, RT15, RT16, RT18, RT19, RT20 model_ft]
The dash post is where all four legs plug in at the dash node, beside the PMU. Its place comes from the dash spaces: low, close to the centre stack, clear of water. [work E13; routes RT11]
The tunnel carries three heavy cables beside the rear leg's bundle: the 2 AWG PMU feed and two 1/0 cables (starter feed and cranking return). Measure it for all of them together. [routes RT15; cables C03, C04, C11]
The heavy cables' lengths in the record are hand guesses: C03 16 ft, C04 18 ft, C11 18 ft, C07 4 ft. [cables C03, C04, C11, C07]
Water: the car leaks at the cowl seam and the windscreen, right above the dash node. Nothing mounts in the lowest 50 mm of the footwell; every wire enters a box from below or with a drip loop. Where the water really goes is looked at today. [rules water-ingress; checks CK04]
The wiper motor, both pop-up motors and the fuel sender can only be bought used: count their pins while you can see them - the removed part is the buying spec. [work C1]
The road-speed sensor is bought only after the thread on the transmission's speedometer drive is measured. [parts P113]
The hatch hinge loop flexes: measure that run with the hatch open. Measure one headlamp side; the other is that plus the crossing. [routes RT18, RT07]
done_when: All 32 runs have a length in feet, the tunnel's tightest gap is noted, CK04 has a sentence and a photo per side, the pins are counted, the boss thread is read, and each of the day's other rows is answered in the app.
if_not: A run cannot be laid because its end point is not decided (a node's place): mark where you would put it, measure to there and say so. A space too small for the bundle, a grommet that is full, water marks where the node should go: write it as found - it is a finding, never softened.
record: Tick C1. In the answer type one line per run (RT01 4.5 ft), then the tunnel gap in mm, the pin counts, the boss thread, and the CK04 sentences. The other measurements go in their own rows.

goal: How the aftermarket head unit, its amplifier and the wideband gauge are joined to the factory wiring today is traced, labelled and written down, with anything else a previous owner added, and the plugs at the radio opening and on the wideband gauge are counted and photographed.
where: behind the dash and at the radio opening, with the dash out
tools:
torch
phone camera
masking tape and a pen, or the label printer (P041)
multimeter on continuity, for a wire that disappears into tape
before:
S1 is done: the dash, the radio and the amplifier are out and every plug is labelled
Battery negative disconnected, as S1 left it
Nothing is cut, unplugged or untaped beyond what S1 already parted
know:
The head unit is aftermarket, spliced in behind the dash by a previous owner; how is not in the record. [steps E28.03; devices DV28]
Its wires by the usual colours: red (ACC), yellow (battery, memory), orange (illumination), black (ground), blue / white (remote, to the amplifier), and the speaker pairs. [devices DV28]
In the new harness the red goes to L3-M 1, the yellow to L3-M 2 through fuse F1, the orange to L3-S1 8 and the black to dash ground. [devices DV28; fuses F1]
The wideband is an AEM 30-0300 X-Series gauge: it has a +12 V wire, a ground, an AEMnet lead ending in a small 2-way plug, and a fixed sensor lead that runs to the exhaust. [devices DV44]
In the new harness the gauge is fed from fuse F20 and its AEMnet pair joins CAN2 at the dash node. [fuses F20; migration MG25]
The migration moves the head unit at MG02 and the wideband at MG25; both steps wait on what this row finds. [migration MG02, MG25; work E28]
Every leg ends in the plug its part needs. The new head unit and the gauge are not factory parts, so each takes its maker's own lead; what matters today is what is on the car to join them to. [D-543; devices DV28, DV44]
done_when: Every wire of the head unit, the amplifier and the wideband has a label at the place it joins the car's wiring, a photograph, and a line saying which factory wire colour it joins and how (plug adaptor, crimp, twisted and taped, tap connector, add-a-fuse).
if_not: A wire cannot be followed to its end without cutting tape or a loom: stop at the tape, label it there and say so. A joint looks burnt, green or loose: photograph it and say which circuit - it is a finding for the car's issues list.
record: Tick V-116 in the app and type the list in the answer: for each wire, its colour, what it joins and how. Add anything else found that is not factory. Then the two plug lines - one line per device id - ways, colour, any mark, which half is on the part, the photo's name, and whether the plug is sound or cracked.

goal: Every space the dash node could use is measured in mm, the PMU has been tried in them, and you know where the wideband gauge hides and that its sensor lead reaches.
where: behind and under the dash, both footwells
tools:
tape measure and steel rule in mm
the PMU itself, to hold in each space
cardboard, a knife and a marker
torch
phone camera and a ruler
before:
S1 is done: the dash, the console and the carpet are out
Battery negative disconnected
This is the first measurement of the day: the dash post's place comes from it
know:
The dash node is the heart of the new harness. On carrier panels cut to these spaces go: the PMU, two busbars, fuse blocks A and B, the inline fuse holders, seven relay sockets (K1, K2, K3, K4, K11, K12, K13), the wake strip, a small perfboard and the hidden wideband gauge. [work E13]
The PMU is 131 x 112 x 32.5 mm. Its 39-way plug locks with a lever that must be free to swing. [S-028 p.8; work E13, E16]
The node's rules: low and close to the floor; the PMU's lever arc clear; 60 mm clear behind every receptacle; the fuse blocks reachable; the PMU stood off for air. [work E13]
Water: nothing mounts in the lowest 50 mm of the footwell, and the PMU's plug faces down or sideways, never up. [rules water-ingress]
Leave panel room for four more 12-way receptacles beside the engine leg's two, for the future engine swap. [work E13]
The wideband gauge (AEM 30-0300) is kept, out of sight, as the sensor's controller. Its sensor lead is a fixed length and is never cut or extended, so where the gauge hides is settled by whether the lead reaches the exhaust bung. [D-244; modules WBO]
The spaces to measure: the centre-stack cavity, the glovebox region, and the floor under the dash on both sides. [work Q-014]
The panel stock is bought after today, cut to cardboard patterns made in the car. [parts P090; work E13]
Nothing here has been measured; fit is assumed and these numbers place the parts. [D-455]
done_when: Width x height x depth in mm for the centre-stack cavity and the glovebox region, the flat floor area each side, a yes or no on the PMU's lever and on 60 mm behind the receptacles, a cardboard pattern of each usable space, and the wideband's hiding place with 'lead reaches' or not.
if_not: No space takes the PMU low with its lever clear: say so and give the best place with what is in the way. The sensor lead does not reach: the gauge's place moves, never the lead - find the nearest place it does reach. Water marks in a space: write it; the node goes elsewhere.
record: Q-014 takes a value: the centre-stack cavity as width x height x depth in mm. In words: the glovebox region's three numbers, the two floor areas, the lever and the 60 mm answers, and where the wideband gauge hides.

goal: You know whether the factory speedometer head has a working speed switch - a wire that pulses to ground as the cable turns - and how many pulses it gives per turn.
where: the bench, with the cluster out, and behind the dash
tools:
multimeter with a continuity beeper
a small screwdriver to turn the speedometer's input
masking tape and a marker
phone camera
before:
The cluster is out and its speedometer cable released (S1)
Battery negative disconnected
know:
The design's road speed today is a bought Hall sensor on the transmission's speedometer drive, the cable deleted, wired through the tunnel on L4-S 3 and L4-S 4. [D-272; parts P113; cavities L4-S 3, L4-S 4]
The 1982 component list carries a vehicle speed switch, B-29: a reed switch inside the speedometer head that pulses to ground on a single BR wire. It fed cruise control. [work Q-115; 00-CAR PT652-B-25_BR]
This GS left the factory without cruise control, so the switch may not be in this speedometer at all. [00-CAR PT649]
If it is there and works, road speed needs one wire from behind the dash to the ICU's speed input, and the tunnel run and the bought sensor are not needed. [work Q-115; D-409; cavities DP-ICU 14]
A spare cavity for it would be one of L3-S3 5 to 8; L3-S2 12 carries the kick-down switch's supply. [cavities L3-S2 12, L3-S3 5]
The speedometer is driven by a cable from the transmission. [00-CAR PT621, PT622]
Pulses per mile is a setting, trued once against a measured mile; today's count only has to show a clean, repeatable pulse. [D-272]
done_when: One of three answers: no switch fitted; a switch that does not pulse; or a switch that pulses N times per turn of the speedometer's input, every turn the same.
if_not: No BR wire and no extra terminal on the speedometer: answer 'not fitted' - the design keeps the transmission sensor. Pulses that come and go: say so; an unreliable switch is the same as none.
record: Tick Q-115. In words: fitted or not, pulses per turn, and where the BR wire ends behind the dash.

goal: The pop-up motors are confirmed against the pin plan: CK08's readings agree with the factory diagram, or the difference is stated, before the front leg is pinned.
where: the nose, at the two pop-up motors
tools:
the CK08 readings from V-114
torch
phone camera
before:
V-114's CK08 is taken: the ohm readings and the powered test on both motors
Battery negative disconnected
know:
Each motor's plug is a four-way, not two wires: WR, YG, R, RY. Cross-shaped, YG at the top, WR left, RY right, R bottom. [00-CAR PT033-WR; D-348]
The diagram: R (up) and RY (down) each go through a diode to a cam switch that drives a relay inside the motor; the relay connects WR to the motor; YG is at 12 V while it runs. [00-CAR SP-584]
The design follows it. One WR feed from output O1 on L2-P 3, split at the nose to both motors, 12 AWG. Up commands on R: L2-S 1 left, L2-S 2 right. Down commands on RY: L2-P 4 left, L2-S 6 right. All four commands 14 AWG. YG capped at each motor. [cavities L2-P 3, L2-P 4, L2-S 1, L2-S 2, L2-S 6; D-487; D-460]
Relays K1 and K2 at the dash node steer 12 V to R or RY, behind a 5 A fuse, F37. [relays K1, K2; fuses F37]
The PMU tells a moving lamp from O1's current: above idle only while a motor turns. CK08's two currents set that threshold. [rules pop-up-cycle; checks CK08]
If the motor is not what the diagram shows - no relay inside, or YG a contact to ground - the leg is re-pinned from the measurement. Do not pin the front leg before this row. [D-487; work V-081]
done_when: You have said 'matches the diagram' or listed what differs, for each motor.
if_not: Any of the four behaviours differs on either motor: do not adjust anything. Write the reading and the lamp position; the agent redraws the drive (R14).
record: Tick V-081. In words, per motor: R raises and stops itself yes/no; RY lowers and stops itself yes/no; YG at 12 V only while moving yes/no; the idle and travelling currents.

goal: The space behind the driver's kick panel is measured in mm, and you know whether a 150 x 100 mm panel fits there.
where: driver's footwell, where the kick panel was
tools:
tape measure and steel rule in mm
a 150 x 100 mm piece of cardboard
torch
phone camera and a ruler
before:
S1 is done: the kick panel and the sill plate are out
Battery negative disconnected
know:
The sill node is a small panel behind the driver's kick panel. It carries the two door receptacles D1 and D2 (8-way Deutsch DT04-8P), a ground stud, four relay sockets for the window relays K5 to K8, and two sealed inline fuse holders, F8 and F9. [work V-055; housings D1, D2; relays K5, K6, K7, K8; fuses F8, F9]
The panel is planned at about 150 x 100 mm; its stock is bought after today. [work V-055; parts P091]
The run to it from the dash post is along the sill; from it a branch goes through each door's jamb boot. [routes RT19, RT20]
Water: nothing mounts in the lowest 50 mm of the footwell. [rules water-ingress]
The dash node allows 60 mm clear behind every receptacle for the wires to leave; the same room is wanted here. [work E13]
While you are here the luxury project wants the diameter of the speaker hole in the kick panel - the cut-out, not the old speaker (luxury V-103). [04-luxury work V-103]
done_when: The flat space's width and height in mm, its depth to the trim, and a yes or no on the 150 x 100 mm card sitting flat there.
if_not: The card does not fit: give the largest rectangle that does and what is in the way. That is the answer; the agent re-plans the sill node.
record: V-055 takes a value: width x height in mm of the usable space. In words: the depth, fits yes / no, and what is in the way. The speaker hole's diameter goes in the luxury row V-103.

goal: A cardboard mock-up shows whether the battery, the amplifier, the Class-T fuse block and the master disconnect fit the cargo bin, and that a hand can reach a battery post to jump-start the car with the boots on.
where: the cargo area: the storage bins behind the seats
tools:
cardboard, a knife, tape and a marker
tape measure in mm
the Ionic battery, terminals taped over
phone camera and a ruler
torch
before:
S1 is done: the bins' trim and lids are out
Rings and watch off around the battery; its posts taped or booted
know:
The battery's case is 170 wide x 230 long x 190 high, in mm, measured 2026-09-04. Its terminals and their boots stand above the 190. [params battery_case_mm; D-239]
It moves to the passenger-side bin; the driver-side bin is kept for the subwoofer. [04-luxury D-449]
In the same bin, on the positive: the master disconnect switch (Blue Sea 9003e), with the Class-T fuse block (Blue Sea 5007100, a 150 A fuse) and two small fuse holders (Blue Sea 5191) fed from its output stud; and the new amplifier. [parts P049, P047, P051; backbone B1, B2, B8]
Battery post to switch to fuses stays within inches: the record guesses 1 ft each for those two cables. [cables C12, C01]
The battery has tapered posts: brass clamps with a 3/8 in stud go on them, covered by pull-off boots and nothing else. There is no cover panel, on purpose, so a jump start only needs a boot pulled off. [D-235; parts P094, P095]
It is held by a hold-down clamp with J-hooks and M8 hardware on a backing plate; the plate's stock is sized from this mock-up. [parts P057, P092]
The negative goes straight to a ground stud on bare metal near the battery, on a 1/0 cable guessed at 3 ft. [backbone B5; cables C05]
The amplifier is not chosen yet, so its size is unknown; its cable is sized for the largest class considered. [cables C13; 04-luxury D-449]
The sizes of the switch and the fuse block are not in the record. [parts P049, P047 - no dimensions]
Whether the amplifier's fuse holder stacks on the switch's output stud or sits on a short lead is settled here. [parts P051]
done_when: A photo of the mock-up in the bin, the bin's inside size in mm, and a yes or no to: everything fits; a hand reaches each post with the boots on; the lid closes.
if_not: It does not all fit in one bin: say what is left over and how much room the other bin has. A post cannot be reached: move the mock battery until it can and note the position. Do not decide for a tighter fit - give the numbers.
record: Tick V-088. In words: the bin's length x width x depth in mm, fits yes / no, reach yes / no, lid yes / no, and where the ground stud and the cable exit would go.

goal: You know what works in the two releases - each dash switch and each solenoid - and exactly what is broken in the hatch latch switch.
where: the removed dash switches on the bench, the hatch lock, and the fuel-door solenoid behind the left rear trim
tools:
multimeter on ohms / continuity
torch
screwdrivers
phone camera
before:
S1 is done: the dash switches are unplugged and the cargo trim is out
V-114's CK20 is taken: each solenoid's current, with the car whole
Battery negative disconnected: this row is all ohm readings
know:
The factory circuit: a 20 A always-live fuse feeds wire LR to both dash switches. The hatch switch (H-13) sends GR to the hatch solenoid; the fuel-door switch (H-15) sends GB to its solenoid. Both solenoids ground on a B wire at the rear ground point X-15. [00-CAR PT030-GR, PT030-B, PT031-GB, PT031-B, PT635-LR, PT635-GB, SP-218]
The new design keeps both solenoids and feeds them on new wires: L4-M 3 to the hatch and L4-M 4 to the fuel door, 14 AWG, through relays K3 and K4 at the dash node behind a 10 A fuse, F33. [cavities L4-M 3, L4-M 4; relays K3, K4; fuses F33; D-451]
Each solenoid keeps its own factory ground; its continuity to the body is to be confirmed. [devices DV48, DV49]
The hatch latch switch is broken; the solenoid itself is fitted and believed to work. [00-CAR K-016; devices DV48]
The 1985 manual's figure of the hatch lock shows a switch built into the lock body, with contact points A and B beside the key cylinder. Whether the 1982 lock is the same is not confirmed. [00-CAR PT812; S-002 p.14-12]
A replacement latch switch (P165) is bought only once this row confirms the switch is what is broken. [parts P165]
Hatch solenoid: owners report its inner rubber bumpers crumble and jam it. It unbolts with its rod off the latch and two screws in its rubber boot. [00-CAR PT030]
Fuel door: its manual release is a slide at the top of the mechanism, pushed rearward, behind the left rear speaker cover or under the cargo carpet. Never pry the lid from outside. [00-CAR PT031]
The wire colours at the latch switch are not in the record. [00-CAR PT812 - no terminals listed]
done_when: Six answers: hatch switch works yes / no; fuel-door switch works yes / no; hatch solenoid fires yes / no; fuel-door solenoid fires yes / no; each solenoid's ground under 1 ohm to the body; and what exactly is broken in the latch switch.
if_not: A solenoid that did not fire at CK20: say so here and do not open it up today. The latch switch cannot be found on the lock: photograph the lock from every side and say so.
record: Tick V-112. In words: the six answers, the latch switch's wire colours, and any number printed on it.

goal: You have ruled the design verified - the freeze. The project moves to SOURCING and the build list opens.
where: desk, in the app
time: an evening to read; a minute to answer
tools: the Rx7 app
before:
Z1, the design review, is done with no Blocker or Major finding left open
The agent has raised the design-freeze block and it shows in the app
know:
The freeze is the one gate between the design list and the build list: every build row waits on it, and only your answer moves it. [D-386; rx7.py doc work]
Your own rule: nothing is bought until the plan is 'detail for detail flawless' and you understand it as if it were already in the car and working. [D-323]
The review is four separate readers - a designer, a buyer who never sees the design, a builder who only follows instructions, and an auditor. Every finding became a work row or a block. [work Z1; rx7.py playbook review]
A Blocker or Major finding reopens the design list; the freeze is not asked for while one is open. [work Z1]
The freeze does not close design. A design row opened afterwards holds only the build rows it changes. [rx7.py doc work]
What it unlocks first is money: the four carts stood at $455.04, $382.68, $944.08 and $1,096.22 at their last review, about $2,878 together, to be re-read before paying. [carts]
The car is already apart and stays so through the sourcing and the whole build, until the interior goes back. [D-387; work E35]
done_when: The freeze block is answered, the agent has applied it, and the app shows the electrical project at SOURCING with build rows ready.
if_not: Something in the design is still unclear to you: do not freeze. Ask in the app's Discuss chat, or answer the block with what is unclear; the agent opens a design row for it. A freeze given in doubt costs parts bought twice.
record: Answer the design-freeze block in the app: its letter, or 'follow the recommendation', with any words you want kept. That answer is this row; then press Apply.
